pillar_reactions.evidence: Volunteered a positive reaction and tied it directly to his own stated goal of not needing a coach forever: 'I think it's a really good idea also to, you know, give six months to a year and to set like kind of deadline to teach people. Because that's also why I'm not being consistent... It's good if you guys can also teach me how to build it up by myself, which I can keep going later. I think that's a really good philosophy, actually.' The teach-you-to-leave framing landed harder than the training content itself.

Reacted positively and contrasted it favourably against the rigid plans he associates with coaching: 'I like this idea because most of the time it's like you have a really strict line which is like protein, chicken, and rice, right? Which most of the people, no one likes it so everyone is leaving it out.' He also volunteered that his job makes compliance easy — 'I can order whatever I want and then I have a whole kitchen so I have everything near me' — while naming nutrition as his real gap: 'I need you guys to help me to know where to go... to be frank, it's never been focused for me.'

Asked a question to confirm the mechanics rather than reacting to the value: 'So it's like, it's going to be like a tailor-made weekly program, depending on our communication, basically.' The rep confirmed and extended. No objection and no enthusiasm — he was checking he had understood how the weekly check-ins and WhatsApp access actually worked across a time zone.

anchors.raw: No, but, like, to be totally honest with you, I was expecting, like, kind of a monthly rating, right?
anchors.note: The prospect arrived expecting a monthly subscription, not a lump sum, and had budgeted nothing: 'I didn't plan any amount or anything about this.' This is the anchor that actually governed the outcome — the $6,000 was not rejected on value but on shape. It is a recurring pattern worth watching: a prospect who accepts the programme fully and stalls purely on billing structure.

anchors.raw: I've been doing some coach training with a guy called Maverick last year or two years ago, which I follow the program a few times, but like I had to stop and then he just stopped the app.
anchors.competitor: Maverick (app-based kettlebell coaching programme, since discontinued)
anchors.note: No price was ever stated for this product, so the magnitude of the anchor is unknown, but an app-based programme is the reference point he brought to the call and is consistent with his monthly-billing expectation. Recorded because it is the product in his head when he hears $6,000, not because a number was given.

unmet_demand.want: To pay monthly rather than in a lump sum up front
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep never presented a structured instalment option. He floated 'we can do half-half' without terms and then substituted a $100-$200 reversible holding deposit with the balance deferred, leaving the prospect without an actual plan to say yes to.

unmet_demand.want: Coaching responsive across a Hong Kong time zone, around 8am-to-midnight kitchen shifts
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Partially addressed rather than unmet — the rep offered WhatsApp access and flagged the lag honestly ('because you're in a different time zone, it might take a little bit longer sometimes for him to respond'). Whether a single coach can service this schedule is untested.
